plan.title: fix(scope-provenance): one-PR gate crashes with ENOBUFS when PROJECT-DEFINITION exceeds 1 MiB

narratives.Description: The #6273 one-PR gate reads PROJECT-DEFINITION at the merge base through a git helper with Node's 1 MiB default maxBuffer; this repo's PROJECT-DEFINITION is over 1 MiB, so verify:scope-provenance fails with ENOBUFS. This story gives that helper, and the one other core reader of PROJECT-DEFINITION at a ref without a buffer (coverage-applicability), the shared 64 MiB SUBPROCESS_MAX_BUFFER, with a real-git regression test.
narratives.Overview:
## Summary

The #6273 one-PR gate crashes on its first real use. `verify:scope-provenance` reads `xbrief/PROJECT-DEFINITION.xbrief.json` at the merge base with `git show <base>:<path>`, through a `spawnSync` helper with no `maxBuffer`, so Node uses its 1 MiB default. This repository PROJECT-DEFINITION is 1,092,574 bytes, so the read fails:

`git show 47b312c47:xbrief/PROJECT-DEFINITION.xbrief.json failed: spawnSync git ENOBUFS`

The path (`resolveOnePrGate` to `readPolicyAtMergeBase`) runs only when a same-PR approval record exists. #6327 is the first such PR, and the #6273 tests use seams, so nothing caught it. Pinned 0.129.9 has the bug, so CI fails the same way.

## Expected

- The `git()` helper in `packages/core/src/scope-provenance/evaluate.ts` sets `maxBuffer: 64 * 1024 * 1024`, the same as `forge-approval.ts` in the same folder.
- Other readers that run `git show <ref>:xbrief/PROJECT-DEFINITION.xbrief.json` get the same limit (intent-constraint and observable-scope are the known candidates; check the rest).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a merge base whose PROJECT-DEFINITION is larger than 1 MiB, when `verify:scope-provenance` runs on a one-PR change set with a valid approval record, then it reads the policy and admits or refuses on the policy, not on ENOBUFS.
- A regression test reads a blob larger than 1 MiB through the real git helper, not a seam.
- Every `git show` reader of PROJECT-DEFINITION in core uses the larger buffer.

Blocks #6327. Refs #6273. Refs #6346.
narratives.UserStory: As a maintainer using the one-PR mint route, I want verify:scope-provenance to read a PROJECT-DEFINITION larger than 1 MiB at the merge base, so that the gate admits or refuses on the policy instead of crashing with ENOBUFS.
narratives.ImplementationPlan:
1. packages/core/src/scope-provenance/evaluate.ts: the `git()` helper passes `maxBuffer: SUBPROCESS_MAX_BUFFER` (../subprocess/max-buffer.js, 64 MiB, the value forge-approval.ts uses).
2. packages/core/src/coverage-applicability/evaluate.ts: `defaultRunGit` passes the same maxBuffer; it reads PROJECT-DEFINITION at the base and head SHA for the registry-refresh demotion, which today silently stays coverable on ENOBUFS.
3. packages/core/src/scope-provenance/evaluate-git.test.ts: real-git fixture whose merge-base PROJECT-DEFINITION is over 1 MiB (onePrScopeProof mint, requireHumanMerge true) with a same-PR minted record; no read seam; assert no ENOBUFS and the policy decides. packages/core/src/coverage-applicability/evaluate.test.ts: a registry-refresh-only change to a PROJECT-DEFINITION over 1 MiB is demoted.
4. One CHANGELOG.md [Unreleased] line.
Other core readers of PROJECT-DEFINITION at a ref already set 10 MiB or more (class-checks, intent-constraint, observable-scope, pre-push, session/git for branch-sync); no change there.

narrative.Acceptance: Given the core readers that run `git show <ref>:xbrief/PROJECT-DEFINITION.xbrief.json`, then each passes a maxBuffer of at least 10 MiB; scope-provenance/evaluate.ts and coverage-applicability/evaluate.ts gain `SUBPROCESS_MAX_BUFFER` (64 MiB).
